Prunlet — Windows Recycle Bin deletion a: Prunlet — Windows Recycle Bin deletion and registry recovery.
Legacy --allowed-root <directory> option: Legacy --allowed-root <directory> options are accepted but do not restrict target directories.
Metadata and volume recovery directories: Metadata and volume recovery directories are protected.
Files and folders normally move into the: Files and folders normally move into the Windows Recycle Bin without Prunlet operation records.
An ordinary file with a Windows reserved: An ordinary file with a Windows reserved final name is permanently deleted after identity checks, without using the bin.
Dry-run reports that case as would_perma: Dry-run reports that case as would_permanently_delete. Reserved-name directories and links are rejected.
When Windows reports a file or folder to: When Windows reports a file or folder too large for the bin, Prunlet attempts to permanently delete its confirmed original.
Only a confirmed removal returns permane: Only a confirmed removal returns permanently_deleted; an uncertain attempt returns ambiguous.
On a volume whose confirmed immediate-de: On a volume whose confirmed immediate-delete setting means the bin is unavailable, an item may also be permanently deleted after the same identity checks; its status is permanently_deleted, never recycled.
Other recycling failures do not trigger: Other recycling failures do not trigger permanent deletion. Dry-run cannot predict an ordinary item's bin-size outcome.
Restore recycled items using Windows Rec: Restore recycled items using Windows Recycle Bin; permanently deleted items cannot be restored there.
Registry snapshots retain the configured: Registry snapshots retain the configured 7-day / 1 GiB defaults.
Maintain and purge manage registry recov: Maintain and purge manage registry recovery only; inspection is the default.
Migrate discards owned legacy file recov: Migrate discards owned legacy file recovery data through Windows Recycle Bin; registry recovery stays protected.
After checking an interrupted discard, u: After checking an interrupted discard, use migrate --apply --retry-legacy-discard to explicitly acknowledge retry.
Restore and registry-restore accept regi: Restore and registry-restore accept registry operation IDs and never overwrite existing keys or values.
Recycled hard links share content with s: Recycled hard links share content with surviving aliases.
For ambiguous file results, inspect the: For ambiguous file results, inspect the source and Windows Recycle Bin; do not resend deletion.
Empty directories are supported; deletin: Empty directories are supported; deleting directory contents requires --recursive.
Wildcard expansion is unsupported. Links: Wildcard expansion is unsupported. Links are deleted without following their targets.
Registry view is required. Omit value-na: Registry view is required. Omit value-name for a key; an empty value-name selects the default value.
Registry access defaults to normal. back: Registry access defaults to normal. backupRestore is explicit per deletion/restoration, requires effective-token privileges, and supports only view 64 in a 64-bit Windows process.
Registry key snapshots require full Owne: Registry key snapshots require full Owner/Group/DACL/SACL access and SeSecurityPrivilege; no automatic elevation or fallback.
